Gold: 1 = 100 crowns. deadline: seasons the King has to answer a card from its rider's arrival (a card's own deadline overrides), then it lapses and doing nothing costs. rider.speed: tiles a season the rider rides from the card's town to the King's seat (the card is seen coming, riding, and not answered until he arrives).

cards.subject: house_warm

{house} decides the King has no judgement to give.
{house} concludes the King has no judgement to offer.
{house} decides the crown will not judge.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {rival} holds {house}'s knights
cards.text: A dozen knights of {house} sit in {rival}'s cells. {lord} begs the King to buy them out.

choices.label: Pay the ransom
text: The knights ride home to {town} on the crown's silver.
The crown's silver brings the knights home to {town}.
The knights return to {town}, ransomed by the King.

choices.label: Order {rival} to free them
text: The King's order goes to {rival}.
{rival} receives the King's order.
The order goes out to {rival}.
{rival} frees half the knights, and keeps the rich ones.
{rival} lets half the knights go, keeping the wealthy ones.
Half the knights come home; {rival} holds the rich.

choices.label: A war's prisoners are a war's business
text: {lord} goes home empty-handed.
{lord} rides home with nothing.
Empty-handed, {lord} leaves.
{house}'s knights rot in {rival}'s cells.
The knights of {house} waste away in {rival}'s cells.
{rival}'s cells hold {house}'s knights, rotting.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} and {rival} fight over a ford
cards.text: One crossing on the river, two houses that want it. Every week a few more men drown in it.

choices.label: Give the ford to the crown
text: The King's men hold the ford; both houses pay to cross.
The crown holds the ford, and both houses pay to cross it.
Royal men keep the ford; each house pays its crossing.
The ford's tolls come to Kingsmere every season.
Every season, the ford's tolls arrive at Kingsmere.
Kingsmere collects the ford tolls season by season.

choices.label: Give it to {house}
text: {house} holds the ford by the King's grant.
The ford belongs to {house} by royal grant.
By the King's grant, {house} keeps the ford.

choices.label: Build a second bridge
text: Masons build a bridge upriver; neither house need fight.
Upriver, masons raise a bridge, and neither house need fight.
A second bridge goes up, leaving nothing to fight over.
The ford runs red every spring.
Each spring the ford runs red.
The ford is bloodied every spring.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: A peace feast for {house} and {rival}
cards.text: A herald says both houses are tired. A feast at the King's table might end it, or start it again over the wine.

choices.label: Host the feast
text: {house} and {rival} drink at Kingsmere, swords at the door.
{house} and {rival} share wine at Kingsmere, their swords left at the door.
Swords at the door, {house} and {rival} drink together at Kingsmere.
The peace made at the King's table holds through the season.
The peace sworn at the King's table lasts the season.
What was agreed over the King's wine holds for the season.

choices.label: Make them swear on the relics
text: Both lords swear peace before the gods.
Before the gods, both lords swear to keep the peace.
The two lords take oath on the relics.

choices.label: Let them bleed
text: The King has better uses for wine.
The King finds better things to do with his wine.
No feast; the King's wine is kept for better use.
The war goes on; the herald goes home.
The herald returns home, and the war continues.
The war rolls on, and the herald goes back.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} sends the King a share of plunder
cards.text: {lord} has sacked one of {rival}'s villages and sends the crown a cart of silver plate.

choices.label: Take it
text: The plate goes to the treasury; {rival} hears of it.
The treasury takes the plate, and {rival} hears about it.
{rival} learns its plate now sits in the King's treasury.

choices.label: Send it back to {rival}
text: The plate goes home to {rival} with the King's regrets.
The plate returns to {rival} along with the King's apologies.
With the King's regrets, {rival} gets its plate back.

choices.label: Give it to the burned village
text: The village gets its plate back, and a new roof.
The village has its plate again, and a new roof as well.
The burned village gets back its plate, and a roof besides.
The village tells everyone the King is just.
The village tells all comers that the King is just.
The King's justice is the village's favourite tale.
The plate sits in the courtyard; everyone knows whose it was.
The plate lies in the courtyard, and all know its owner.
Nobody touches the plate in the courtyard; everyone knows whose it is.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} asks leave to go to war
cards.text: {house} has an old grudge against a neighbour, and {lord} wants the King's blessing to settle it.

choices.label: Give your blessing
text: {lord} rides out with the King's leave.
With the King's leave, {lord} rides to war.
{lord} rides out, blessed by the crown.
{house} comes home with new fields, and new enemies.
{house} returns with new fields and new foes.
New lands for {house}, and new enemies with them.

choices.label: Forbid it
text: {lord} sheathes the sword, for now.
{lord} puts away the sword, for the present.
The sword goes back in its scabbard; {lord} waits.

choices.label: Settle the grudge at court
text: The King hears both houses and splits the difference.
The King hears both houses and divides the difference.
At court, the grudge is heard and split down the middle.
{lord} goes to war without asking.
{lord} marches to war unasked.
Without the King's leave, {lord} goes to war.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Bread riot in {town}
cards.text: The bakers of {town} have no flour and the crowd thinks they are lying. Ovens are being smashed. {house}'s men stand by.

choices.label: Send grain and soldiers
text: Carts and spears roll into {town} together. {house} sees order and bread.
Grain and spearmen. {house} thanks the King.

choices.label: Soldiers only
text: The King's men clear {town}'s streets with staves. {house} watches.
Staves, not bread. {house} remembers.
{town} remembers the staves at harvest, and so does {house}.
{house} says the King beat its people.

choices.label: Throw open {house}'s barns
text: {house}'s barns are opened by the King's word. {lord} is furious; the other lords approve.
{town} eats {house}'s grain on the King's order.
{town} burns its bakeries. {house} blames the crown.
The riot spreads. {house} says the King let it.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} sends its children away
cards.text: Mothers in {town} put their children on carts to anywhere with bread. {house} has done nothing.

choices.label: Take them in at Kingsmere
text: {town}'s children fill the King's halls. {house} is shamed, and the other houses see it.
The King feeds {house}'s children. {lord} hears of it.
{town}'s children grow up loyal to the King, not {house}.
The boys raised at Kingsmere join the royal host.

choices.label: Send bread to {town}
text: Bread carts meet the children on the road. {house} is grateful.
The children go home to bread. {house} thanks the crown.

choices.label: Close the roads
text: The children turn back. {house} sees the King shut them out.
The roads close. {lord} curses the crown.
The children of {town} scatter. {house} blames the King.
{town}'s children go where they can.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} eats its warhorses
cards.text: The last horses in {town} are going into the pot, {house}'s warhorses among them. No horses, no knights next year.

choices.label: Send grain so the horses live
text: Grain reaches {town}. {house}'s knights keep their horses.
The horses are spared. {house} can still ride for the King.

choices.label: Buy the horses for the royal host
text: The King buys {house}'s warhorses. {town} eats; {house} walks.
Royal silver for {house}'s horses. The host gains riders.

choices.label: Let them eat
text: {town} eats tonight. {house} has no knights next year.
The horses go into the pot.
{house} can't field its knights. It blames the King.
{house} sends no horsemen to the muster.
{town} eats its horses and its seed corn. {house} blames the crown.
No horses at {town}.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Terrible rumours from {town}
cards.text: Travellers whisper about what the starving of {town} eat now. Every hall says {house} let it happen.

choices.label: Send the royal granary's last
text: The last of the crown's grain goes to {town}. {house} is in the King's debt.
{town} is fed from Kingsmere. {house} owes the crown.

choices.label: Shame {house} for it before the court
text: {lord} is named before the lords. {house} burns.
The court hears what {house} let happen.

choices.label: Close {town} to travellers
text: {town} is sealed. The tales grow worse.
No one enters {town}. {house} is left alone with it.
The tales from {town} reach every hall. The King looks cruel, {house} worse.
Every telling is worse than the last.
The whispers about {town} reach every hall.
{house}'s name is cursed, and the King's beside it.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {house} bids against the crown for a grain ship
cards.text: A southern captain has a hold full of wheat. {lord} of {house} is bidding for it too.

choices.label: Outbid {house}
text: The crown pays more. The wheat goes to the hungry. {house} loses the bid.
The wheat is the King's. {lord} is annoyed.

choices.label: Let {house} have it
text: {house} buys the grain and feeds its own lands. {lord} thanks the King for stepping aside.
{house} gets the wheat.

choices.label: Seize the ship
text: The captain is put ashore; the wheat is the crown's. {house} thinks the King a pirate.
The crown takes the cargo.
No southern ship will dock in the King's harbours.
The southern ships shun the King's ports.
The ship sails to {house}'s harbour instead.
{house} buys the grain.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Deserters on the roads
cards.text: Men are slipping away from the levies with their spears. Some go home; some go into the woods.

choices.label: Hang the deserters you catch
text: Gibbets go up at the crossroads.
Gibbets rise at the crossroads.
The crossroads get their gibbets.

choices.label: Pay the levy on time
text: The crown's pay chests ride out to every camp.
Pay chests from the crown reach every camp.
Every camp is paid on time from the crown's chests.

choices.label: Let the farmers go home
text: The levy thins; the fields fill.
The levy shrinks, and the fields are full of hands.
Farmers go home; fewer spears, more ploughs.
A thin levy meets the trouble.
The trouble is met by a thin levy.
Only a thin levy stands against the trouble.
The deserters become bandits.
The deserters turn to banditry.
Bandits are what the deserters become.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A spy from the enemy camp
cards.text: A man was taken near the walls with a map of Kingsmere's gates sewn into his coat.

choices.label: Make him talk
text: The spy talks; the King learns the enemy's numbers.
The spy speaks, and the King learns how many the enemy are.
Under questioning, the spy gives up the enemy's numbers.

choices.label: Send him back with a false map
text: The spy goes home with the wrong gates.
The spy returns home with the gates all wrong.
A false map rides home with the spy.
The enemy's men come to the wrong gate.
The enemy arrives at the wrong gate.
The wrong gate is where the enemy comes.

choices.label: Hang him from the gate
text: The spy hangs where his friends can see him.
The spy hangs in sight of his friends.
From the gate the spy hangs, for his friends to see.
The spy slips his ropes in the night.
In the night, the spy gets out of his ropes.
The spy is gone by morning, his ropes empty.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Kingsmere's walls are old
cards.text: The master mason says the north wall is more ivy than stone. With trouble coming, someone should mend it.

choices.label: Mend it now, whatever the cost
text: Masons swarm the north wall.
The north wall crawls with masons.
Masons descend on the north wall in numbers.

choices.label: Patch the worst of it
text: Timber and earth fill the cracks.
The cracks are stuffed with timber and earth.
Earth and timber plug the worst of the gaps.

choices.label: The walls have stood a hundred years
text: The ivy stays.
The ivy is left alone.
Nobody touches the ivy.
The north wall slumps in the rain.
In the rain, the north wall sags.
Rain brings the north wall slumping down.
The north wall crumbles a little more.
A little more of the north wall falls away.
The north wall crumbles on, a stone at a time.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords sit on their hands
cards.text: With trouble on the march, the great houses send letters full of excuses and no spears.

choices.label: Shame them in open court
text: The King reads their letters aloud at Kingsmere.
At Kingsmere, the King reads their letters out loud.
Their letters are read before the whole court by the King.

choices.label: Buy their spears
text: Silver goes out; spears come in.
Silver leaves the treasury, and spears arrive.
The crown pays, and the lords' spears come.

choices.label: Fight without them
text: The crown stands alone.
The crown faces it by itself.
Alone, the crown takes the field.
The lords who held back now say the King needed no help.
The lords who hung back now claim the King never needed them.
Having stayed home, the lords now say the King managed fine without them.
The lords wait to see who wins.
The lords bide their time to see who prevails.
The lords hold back and watch for the winner.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: An old enemy's son comes to court
cards.text: The son of a lord the King once broke asks to serve. He smiles a great deal.

choices.label: Take him into service
text: He serves, and smiles.
He serves, smiling.
The son takes service, still smiling.
The son serves faithfully; the old feud is buried.
The son serves loyally, and the old feud is laid to rest.
The feud is buried; the son proves faithful.

choices.label: Watch him closely
text: A spy sleeps outside the son's door.
A spy beds down outside the son's door.
The son sleeps with a spy at his door.

choices.label: Send him away
text: The son leaves, still smiling.
The son goes, smiling still.
Sent away, the son leaves with his smile intact.
The son is seen at a cold house's table.
The son is seen dining with a cold house.
A cold house has the son at its table.
The son finds another lord to serve.
The son takes service with another lord.
Another lord gains the son's service.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A southern prince offers an alliance
cards.text: A prince from beyond the hills sends an envoy: spears for the King's wars, ports for his ships.

choices.label: Sign the alliance
text: The King's seal goes on the treaty.
The treaty bears the King's seal.
The King seals the alliance.
The southern prince calls on the alliance; the crown must send men.
The southern prince invokes the alliance, and the crown must send men.
Men must march south; the prince has called on the treaty.

choices.label: Trade only, no spears
text: A trading treaty is signed.
A treaty of trade is signed.
The crown signs for trade alone.
Southern ships fill the King's ports with goods.
The King's ports fill with goods from southern ships.
Southern ships crowd the harbours with cargo.

choices.label: No foreign ties
text: The envoy goes home.
The envoy returns home.
Home goes the envoy.
The southern prince signs with a great house instead.
The southern prince makes his treaty with a great house.
A great house signs with the southern prince in the King's place.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} says the crown hoards grain
cards.text: {lord} of {house} is telling every hall that Kingsmere's granaries are full while the realm goes hungry.

choices.label: Open the granaries to {house}
text: {house}'s carts fill at Kingsmere. {lord} stops talking.
The crown feeds {house}. The rumour dies.

choices.label: Show {lord} the empty granaries
text: {lord} is walked through bare barns.
{house} sees for itself.

choices.label: Call {lord} a liar
text: The King calls {lord} a liar in front of the court. {house} won't forget.
{house} is shamed. The other lords take sides.
The rumour becomes the truth people tell. {house} gains friends.
Every hall believes {house}.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: A wedding ends in blood at {town}
cards.text: At a wedding in {house}'s hall, an old feud came out with the wine. Two guests are dead.

choices.label: Send the King's justice
text: A royal judge rides to {town}.
A judge of the King's rides to {town}.
{town} receives a royal judge.
The killers hang; {house} says the King's justice is fair.
The killers hang, and {house} calls the King's justice fair.
{house} watches the killers hang, and says the crown judged fairly.

choices.label: Leave it to {lord}
text: {lord} judges in their own hall.
{lord} sits in judgement in their own hall.
In their own hall, {lord} gives judgement.

choices.label: Fine every family there
text: Every family at the wedding pays the crown.
Each family at the wedding pays the crown.
The crown fines every family that attended.
The feud spreads through {house}'s lands.
The feud spreads across the lands of {house}.
{house}'s lands are caught up in the feud.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {house}'s monastery on the war road
cards.text: {lord} would found a monastery near {town}, on the land where the royal host camps on its way north.

choices.label: Be its patron
text: The King endows it. The monks feed his host when it passes.
A royal monastery on the war road. {house} is honoured.

choices.label: Let {house} have the honour
text: {house} builds it. {lord} is pleased.
The monastery is {house}'s.

choices.label: The host needs that land
text: {lord} is refused. The host keeps its camp.
No monastery. {house} is offended.
{house} builds anyway, on the host's camp.
{lord} builds without asking.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} shelters a preacher against the King
cards.text: A preacher at {town}, {lord}'s guest, says the King's crown is cursed and his war is a sin. {house}'s men listen.

choices.label: Demand they hand him over
text: {lord} gives up the preacher. {house} resents it.
The preacher comes to Kingsmere in chains. {house} loses face.

choices.label: Let him preach
text: The preacher goes on. {house}'s men stay home from the muster.
The sermons grow. {house}'s levy shrinks.
{house} uses the preacher's words to refuse the King's call.
{lord} says his men won't fight in a cursed war.

choices.label: Pay the preacher to bless the war
text: The preacher changes his sermon. {house} is puzzled.
Silver turns the curse into a blessing.
The preacher's words spread from {town}.
{house}'s men stop answering the King's call.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers a champion
cards.text: {house} has a giant of a knight, and {lord} would see him fight under the King's banner.

choices.label: Make him the King's champion
text: The giant stands at the King's right hand.
The giant takes his place at the King's right hand.
At the King's right hand stands the giant.

choices.label: Let him fight in the lists
text: The giant unhorses every knight in the realm.
Every knight in the realm is unhorsed by the giant.
The giant knocks each knight of the realm from his saddle.

choices.label: The King has knights enough
text: The giant goes home to {town}.
The giant returns home to {town}.
Back to {town} goes the giant.
The giant fights for a rival court.
A rival court gets the giant's sword.
The giant takes service at a rival court.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: Rats in the host's grain
cards.text: The quartermaster brings a sack gnawed through. Half the host's winter grain is fouled. {house}'s barns at {town} are full.

choices.label: Buy {house}'s grain at its price
text: {house} sells the grain dear and counts the King a good customer.
The carts come from {town}. {house} is paid, and pleased.

choices.label: Take it from {house}'s barns
text: The King's men empty the barns at {town}. {lord} watches and says nothing.
{house}'s grain goes to the host. {lord} keeps a tally.
{lord} still speaks of the barns at {town}.
At {town} they call it the King's theft.

choices.label: Short rations for the host
text: The men eat half and march slower.
The host tightens its belts. The sergeants grumble.
The host goes hungry, and the lords see it.
Hungry soldiers desert, and every house hears of it.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: The bridge on the war road is down
cards.text: Floods took the bridge below {town}. Without it the host marches three days round to reach {house}'s lands.

choices.label: Rebuild it in stone
text: Masons and the crown's silver. The war road is open by the next season.
The bridge goes up in stone. {house} gets a road to the King, and the King one to {house}.

choices.label: Make {house} rebuild it
text: {lord} builds the bridge, slowly, and sends the bill to no one.
{house} rebuilds it at its own cost, and remembers it.

choices.label: March the long way
text: The host goes round. Three days lost each way.
The long road it is. The captains curse the river.
No bridge. Every march to {house}'s lands takes three days longer.
The war road stays cut, and the host's carts cost more each season.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: Snow cuts off {house}
cards.text: The passes to {town} are shut. {house}'s people are eating seed corn, and {lord} has not asked the King for help.

choices.label: Send the host's wagons with grain
text: The King's wagons break through the snow to {town}. {lord} did not ask, and did not expect it.
Grain reaches {town} under the King's banner. {house} talks of it all winter.
{lord} sends men to the spring muster, unasked.
Spring comes and {house}'s spears come with it.

choices.label: Let {lord} come and ask
text: Nobody comes. {house} eats its seed corn.
{lord} is too proud to ask. {town} starves quietly.

choices.label: Send soldiers to guard the passes instead
text: Royal spears hold the passes. {house} sees soldiers, not bread.
The King watches the passes. {lord} reads it as a threat.
{house} comes through the winter without the King, and says so.
Spring finds {house} thinner and colder to the crown.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: Deserters rob {house}'s road
cards.text: Men who ran from the King's levy are robbing carts on the road to {town}. {lord} wants to know whose men they are.

choices.label: Hang them at the crossroads
text: Twelve men hang by the road to {town}. {house} sees the King keeps order.
The deserters hang. {lord} rides past them and nods.

choices.label: Pardon them back into the host
text: The deserters are marched back to the colours.
Back into the ranks they go, with a sergeant at their backs.
{lord} says the King pardons thieves when he needs spears.
{house} has not forgotten its robbed carts.

choices.label: Let {house} deal with them
text: {lord} hangs them himself, and asks why the King's men needed hanging.
{house} does the King's work, and counts it.
The road to {town} stays unsafe, and {house} blames the crown's runaways.
Carts burn on the road to {town}; {house} stops sending its levy money.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: Old soldiers want land
cards.text: Men who fought for the King's father ask for the land they were promised: good fields on {house}'s border.

choices.label: Settle them on {house}'s border
text: Old soldiers farm the border now, with their spears over the door.
A ring of veterans' farms faces {town}. {lord} sees what it is.
The veterans' sons answer the King's levy first.
The border farms send their sons to the muster.

choices.label: Pay them pensions instead
text: Every man gets his pension. The others in the levy take note.
The old soldiers are paid. The young ones see the King pays.

choices.label: That was the old King's promise
text: The old soldiers go home with nothing. The levy hears of it.
Turned away at the gate. The next muster comes up short.
The old soldiers beg at the gate, and the levy sees them there.
Men who bled for the crown sleep in the ditch outside Kingsmere.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: Settlers for the empty march
cards.text: Landless families want the empty land between Kingsmere and {house}. Whoever plants them there owns the border.

choices.label: Plant them under the King's banner
text: A wall of royal farms grows between Kingsmere and {town}.
The march is the King's now. {lord} sees the new fences and counts them.

choices.label: Let {house} settle it
text: {house} plants its own people there. The border moves toward Kingsmere.
{lord} takes the march, and thanks the King for it.
{house}'s new villages raise spears for {house}, not the crown.
The march is {house}'s now, and its levy is {house}'s.

choices.label: Leave it empty
text: The march stays empty. Raiders like it that way.
Nobody farms the march. Only raiders cross it.
The settlers drift to {house}'s lands, and their sons join its levy.
{house} takes the settlers in without asking.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: The river freezes toward {house}
cards.text: The river between Kingsmere and {town} is frozen thick enough for horses. {house} has never been so close.

choices.label: Ride across with the banners
text: The King's horsemen cross the ice and ride past {town}'s walls. {lord} watches from the gate.
Royal banners on the ice below {town}. {house} learns the King can come in winter.

choices.label: Send a herald across with a gift
text: A gift comes over the ice to {town}. {lord} reads it as friendship, or as fear.
{house} gets a royal gift by the ice road, and wonders why now.

choices.label: Let the river thaw
text: The ice melts. The chance goes with it.
Spring comes and the river is a wall again.
The ice melts and nothing crosses it.
The frozen road goes unused.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: The war tax is skimmed in {house}'s lands
cards.text: The crown's collectors in {house}'s lands are taking twice the war tax and keeping half. {lord} says the King robs him.

choices.label: Hang the collectors
text: The collectors hang at {town}. {house} pays its war tax willingly for once.
{lord} watches the King hang his own men, and pays.

choices.label: Return what was taken
text: The silver goes back to {house}, with the King's apology.
{house} gets its silver back. The war chest is thinner.

choices.label: Keep it: the war needs it
text: The silver stays in the war chest. {lord} calls it theft, loudly.
The King keeps the silver. {house} keeps the grudge.
The collectors go on stealing. {house} stops paying altogether.
{lord} sends the collectors home with nothing.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {lord} calls the King a boy
cards.text: At table, {lord} of {house} said the young King has never led a host. The other lords laughed.

choices.label: Hold a muster where {lord} can see it
text: The royal host drills under {town}'s walls for a week. Nobody laughs.
Banners, spears and horses outside {town}. {lord} stops talking.

choices.label: Summon {lord} to kneel
text: {lord} kneels at Kingsmere, and hates it.
{lord} comes, kneels, and rides home angrier.

choices.label: Win {lord} at table
text: The King feasts {lord}. {house} warms. The others call it softness.
A feast for {house}. Some lords think the King is buying friends because he can't win them.
The joke goes round every hall. The lords think the crown is weak.
Nobody answers {lord}. The other houses take note.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {house} holds the coronation's debt
cards.text: {lord} paid for the King's crowning. Now {house} wants the silver back, or a voice in the war council.

choices.label: Pay {house} back
text: The debt is paid. {house} is pleased, and owed nothing.
{lord} takes the silver. The war chest is thinner.

choices.label: Give {lord} a seat at the war council
text: {lord} sits at the war council now. The other houses are not pleased.
{house} has the King's ear. The others want to know why.

choices.label: The crown pays when the war is won
text: {lord} accepts, and watches the war very closely.
{house} waits for a victory to be paid. It wants one soon.
{house} stops waiting and tells the other lords the King is a debtor.
{lord} calls the King a bad debtor in every hall.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: The war chest is empty
cards.text: The steward has counted twice. There is no silver for the next campaign. {house} has silver.

choices.label: Ask {house} for a war loan
text: {lord} lends, and asks to be told where the host marches next.
{house}'s silver fills the war chest. {lord} wants a say in the war.
{lord} wants the loan back, or a town.
{house} reminds the King of what it lent.

choices.label: Raise a war tax on every house
text: Every house pays, and every house grumbles.
The war tax goes out under the King's seal. The lords pay and remember.

choices.label: Melt the royal plate
text: The King's silver plate becomes the host's pay. {lord} thinks the crown is poor.
The plate goes to the melt. The soldiers are paid.
The host goes unpaid. Soldiers start to leave.
No pay. Men slip away from the host by night.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: Silver to spare
cards.text: The war chest is full for once. The steward asks how to spend it. {house} is the house most cold to the crown.

choices.label: Hire spears for the next campaign
text: A company of spears signs the King's book.
The silver buys spears. The other lords see a King who can pay for a war.

choices.label: Send a gift to {house}
text: {lord} takes the gift. Whether {house} reads it as friendship or fear depends on how strong the King looks.
A rich gift reaches {town}. {lord} weighs it, and the King.

choices.label: Keep it for the war
text: The silver stays in the vault. The steward sleeps well.
Kept for the war.
The silver sits in the vault. The lords hear of it, and ask for loans.
Every house hears the crown is rich, and wants a share.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: The steward sells the host's horses
cards.text: The royal steward, a cousin of {house}, has been selling the host's warhorses and sending the silver to {town}.

choices.label: Hang him, cousin or not
text: The steward hangs. {house} mourns him and fears the King.
{lord} buries a cousin. Every house learns the King's horses are not for sale.

choices.label: Make {house} pay for the horses
text: {lord} pays for every horse, and sends the steward to a monastery.
{house} buys the King new warhorses, and keeps quiet.

choices.label: Send him home to {house}
text: The steward goes home. {house} owes the King a favour.
Quietly done. {lord} is grateful. The stables are still empty.
The steward keeps selling. The host has fewer horses each season.
The stables empty, and {town} grows rich.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: The Marshal wants war, the Hand wants terms
cards.text: The Marshal, {house}'s man, wants the host on the road this season. The Hand says the King needs allies first.

choices.label: Back the Marshal
text: The Marshal's war it is. {house} is proud of its man.
{lord} hears the King chose {house}'s man. The host gets ready.

choices.label: Back the Hand
text: Envoys ride out, not soldiers. {house} thinks the King timid.
The Hand's way. {lord} calls it weakness.
The Hand's envoys bring back promises. Some of them will be kept.
Two houses answer the King's envoys kindly.

choices.label: Make them work together
text: They sit at the same table and hate it.
Neither man is happy. The war council goes on.
The two men quarrel in front of the lords. The court looks weak.
Nobody leads the war council. The lords notice.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: The King's cousin and {house}
cards.text: {lord} asks for the King's cousin as a bride for {house}'s heir. A marriage binds a house; it also makes the others jealous.

choices.label: Give her to {house}
text: The wedding is at Kingsmere. {house} is bound to the crown by blood.
{house} has a royal bride. The other lords count the favours.

choices.label: Keep her for a colder house
text: The King keeps his cousin back. {lord} knows why.
{house} is told the King has other plans for her.

choices.label: Ask {house} for spears as her price
text: The bride's price is two hundred spears. {lord} pays it.
{house} sends men to the royal host, and gets a bride.
{lord} finds a bride elsewhere, from a house the King doesn't trust.
{house} marries into another house, not the crown's.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house}'s knights want to change sides
cards.text: Twenty knights who rode for {house} come to Kingsmere. They say {lord} doesn't pay them. They will ride for whoever does.

choices.label: Take them into the royal host
text: Twenty lances ride under the King's banner now. {house} has twenty fewer.
{lord} hears his knights went to the King. He won't forgive it.

choices.label: Send them back to {lord}
text: The knights go home to {town}. {lord} owes the King their loyalty.
{house} gets its knights back, and a reason to trust the King.

choices.label: Pay them to go abroad
text: The knights take the King's silver and ride for the coast.
Twenty lances gone from the realm. Nobody has them.
The knights sell their swords to another house.
Twenty lances go looking for a paymaster. Another lord finds them.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords grow fat in peace
cards.text: No war for a year. The lords feast, quarrel and whisper that the King has no stomach for a fight.

choices.label: Name a campaign against the raiders
text: The King calls the lords to ride against the raiders in spring. Some come gladly.
A campaign is named. The young knights stop drinking and sharpen.

choices.label: Hold a tourney to count the lances
text: Every house sends its knights to the lists. The King counts who comes.
A tourney at Kingsmere. The King learns which houses can field a host.

choices.label: Let them feast
text: The lords feast. The whispers grow.
Peace goes on. The talk of a soft King goes on too.
The lords decide the King is soft, and start making plans.
Peace breeds plots. Two houses meet in secret.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} wants to foster the King's heir
cards.text: {lord} offers to raise the King's heir at {town}, as kings' sons were raised in the old days. It binds {house}. It also puts the heir in {house}'s hands.

choices.label: Send the heir to {town}
text: The heir rides to {town}. {house} is bound to the crown for a generation.
{house} holds the King's son. It is an honour, and a hostage.

choices.label: Ask {house} to send its heir to Kingsmere instead
text: {lord}'s son comes to court. {house} is bound, and watched.
{house} sends its heir. Proud, and not pleased.

choices.label: The heir stays at Kingsmere
text: {lord} is thanked and refused.
The King keeps his son. {house} takes it as a slight.
{lord}'s offer goes unanswered. {house} takes it as an insult.
{house} waits for an answer that never comes.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} shelters a boy with royal blood
cards.text: A boy at {town} says he is the old King's son. He has a ring, an old nurse who backs him, and {house}'s protection.

choices.label: Demand {house} hand him over
text: {lord} sends the boy, and hates the King for it.
The boy comes to Kingsmere under guard. {house} lost its pretender.

choices.label: Pay the nurse to recant
text: The nurse says she was mistaken. {house}'s pretender is a beggar again.
Silver changes the old woman's story. {lord} is left with nothing.

choices.label: Let {house} keep him
text: {house} keeps its boy. The other lords look at the King and wonder.
{lord} has a pretender in his hall, and the King let him keep it.
{house}'s boy grows, and {lord} talks about his claim.
The pretender at {town} has friends now.
The boy at {town} is talked of in every hall.
{house} keeps its claimant, and the realm hears of him.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house}'s man caught raiding
cards.text: The King's men caught a knight of {house} burning a royal village. He says {lord} sent him.

choices.label: Hang him at the gate
text: The knight hangs at Kingsmere. {house} sees the King will fight.
{lord} hears of the rope. The other houses respect it.

choices.label: Ransom him back to {house}
text: {lord} pays for his knight. The village is rebuilt with {house}'s silver.
{house} pays the ransom and pretends it sent no one.

choices.label: Make {lord} come and plead for him
text: {lord} rides to Kingsmere and asks for his man on his knees.
{house} pleads in open court. The King grants it, and everyone saw.
The knight escapes back to {town}. {house} raids again.
Nobody answers. {house} burns another royal village.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house} won't pay the host's tithe
cards.text: {lord} says the crown's reeves counted the sheaves twice. The host needs {house}'s grain this winter.

choices.label: Recount, and take the true tithe
text: The sheaves are counted again. {house} pays what it owes.
A fair count. {lord} pays, sourly.

choices.label: Take the tithe with soldiers
text: Soldiers load {house}'s grain onto the host's carts.
The tithe is taken at spear-point. {house} remembers.

choices.label: Halve it if {house} sends men
text: {house} pays half in grain and half in spearmen.
{lord} keeps his grain and sends his sons.
{house} pays nothing, and the others wonder why they should.
The tithe isn't paid. Two more houses are late.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Maimed soldiers at the gate
cards.text: Men who lost hands and legs in the King's wars beg at {town}'s gate. Every lord who comes to court rides past them.

choices.label: A pension for every man
text: The maimed are paid. The levy sees the King keeps faith with his men.
Pensions for the crippled. More men answer the next muster.

choices.label: Put them to work in the armoury
text: One-handed men can still rivet mail.
The maimed make arrows for the host.

choices.label: Drive them off
text: The maimed are driven from the gate. The levy saw it.
Gone from the gate. The soldiers remember.
The maimed stay at the gate. The lords think the King forgets his soldiers.
Every lord rides past the crippled at the gate.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house}'s young men at the fair
cards.text: At the spring fair the King's sergeants find a hundred young men from {house}'s villages. {lord} wants them for his own levy.

choices.label: Take them into the royal host
text: A hundred young men follow the King's drum. {house}'s levy is smaller.
{lord} hears his villages marched for the King.

choices.label: Send them home to {lord}
text: The young men go home to {house}'s levy.
{lord} keeps his men, and thanks the King.

choices.label: Pay {house} for them
text: {house} sells the King a hundred young men.
Silver for spearmen. {lord} is satisfied.
The young men drink their way home. Nobody gets them.
No one recruits them. The fair ends.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A song about the King who won't fight
cards.text: The taverns sing about a King who hides behind his walls while the raiders burn. The lords' men sing it loudest.

choices.label: Answer it with a campaign
text: The King rides out. The song changes.
A campaign against the raiders. Nobody sings the old song now.

choices.label: Hang the singer
text: One singer hangs. Ten more learn the song.
The singer is hanged. The song goes quiet, and the lords think the King thin-skinned.

choices.label: Let them sing
text: The song spreads to every hall.
They sing it in the great halls now too.
The song reaches every great hall.
The lords laugh at the song, and at the King.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: A dead dog in the muster well
cards.text: Someone threw a dead dog in the well where the royal host musters. Half the men are sick. The camp blames {house}.

choices.label: Blame {house} openly
text: The King names {house}. The other lords believe it.
{lord} is accused before the court. {house} denies it, too late.

choices.label: Find out who really did it
text: The King's men look into it. It was a camp cook with a grudge.
A cook confesses. {house} is spared, and grateful.

choices.label: Dig a new well and say nothing
text: A new well. The host recovers. The rumour doesn't.
The camp drinks clean water. The men still blame {house}.
Sick men leave the host. The camp says {house} did it.
The host loses men to the flux.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: Gold between Kingsmere and {house}
cards.text: Shepherds found gold in the hills where the crown's land meets {house}'s. Both have a claim.

choices.label: Take it for the crown
text: Royal miners dig. The war chest fills. {house} counts every cart.
The gold is the King's. {lord} calls it robbery.

choices.label: Share it with {house}
text: Half to the crown, half to {house}. {lord} is satisfied, for now.
A fair split. {house} likes the King better.

choices.label: Give it to {house}
text: {house} gets the gold. {lord} wonders if the King is generous, or weak.
A gift of a gold mine. The other houses take note.
{house} digs first, and keeps it all.
{lord}'s miners take the gold before the King's arrive.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Clipped coin pays the host
cards.text: The mint at {town} has been clipping the King's silver. The sellswords have noticed, and so have the lords.

choices.label: Hang the mint master
text: The mint master hangs. The coin is honest again.
Honest coin. The sellswords stop complaining.

choices.label: Melt it down and strike it again
text: The war chest pays for good coin.
New coin, full weight. It costs the crown.

choices.label: Keep paying in it
text: The host is paid in short silver. The captains know it.
Clipped coin goes out. The lords hear the crown is cheating.
The sellswords want real silver, or they leave.
A captain throws the King's coin back at the paymaster.
The lords say the King pays in tin.
Clipped coin spreads, and so does the story.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: Salt for the host's winter meat
cards.text: The host needs salt to keep its meat through winter. {house}'s pans at {town} have it, and {lord} knows it.

choices.label: Buy it at {house}'s price
text: {house} sells the salt dear, and likes the King for it.
Royal silver for {house}'s salt. {lord} is pleased.

choices.label: Seize the salt pans
text: The King's men take the pans at {town}. {lord} rages.
The host has salt. {house} has a grudge.

choices.label: The host eats fresh and moves fast
text: No salt. The host lives off the land.
The host forages. The villages suffer.
The host's meat rots. The men go hungry in winter.
No salt. The winter host is weak.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: Good stone near {house}'s border
cards.text: Masons found good stone on the border facing {town}. It would build a fort, and {lord} would see it go up.

choices.label: Build a fort facing {house}
text: A royal fort rises on the border. {house} sees it from its walls.
The fort is built. {lord} knows who it faces.

choices.label: Give the stone to {house}
text: {house} builds with the King's stone. {lord} thanks him.
The stone goes to {town}. {house} is warmer.

choices.label: Sell it
text: The stone goes to the coast. The war chest fills a little.
Sold to merchants.
{house} quarries the stone first and builds its own fort.
{lord}'s masons take the stone.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} sells iron to the King's enemies
cards.text: Smugglers from {town} are selling iron to the King's enemies. {lord} takes a share.

choices.label: Seize the iron
text: The iron is the King's now. {house} lost its share.
The cargo goes to the royal smiths. {lord} says nothing.

choices.label: Take a cut and say nothing
text: The King's share arrives quietly. The other houses hear anyway.
The crown profits. The lords think the King can be bought.

choices.label: Accuse {lord} at court
text: {lord} is named before the lords. {house} burns with shame.
The other lords see {house} trading with the enemy.
The iron goes to the King's enemies. Their spears are better for it.
Smuggled iron arms the King's foes.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: A saint's bones for the banners
cards.text: Monks dug up a saint's bones on {house}'s land. {lord} wants them for {town}. The host wants them carried before it.

choices.label: Carry them before the host
text: The bones go to war with the King. The men fight better for them.
{house} loses its saint. The host gains one.

choices.label: Leave them with {house}
text: The saint stays at {town}. {lord} is grateful.
{house} keeps its relic, and likes the King for it.

choices.label: Give {house} a chapel for them
text: The King pays for a chapel at {town}. {house} is pleased.
A royal chapel for {house}'s saint.
The monks argue; {house} takes the bones by night.
{lord}'s men take the relic. Nobody asked the King.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house}'s bishop wants a greater temple
cards.text: The bishop of {town}, {lord}'s brother, wants silver for a new temple. The war chest needs it too.

choices.label: Pay for the temple
text: The temple at {town} goes up. {house} thanks the King.
The war chest is lighter. {house} is warmer.

choices.label: Ask the bishop to bless the host instead
text: The bishop blesses the King's host. {house} is not impressed.
No temple. A blessing for the soldiers.

choices.label: No silver for temples in wartime
text: The bishop is refused. {lord} hears of it.
The war comes first. {house} grumbles.
The bishop preaches against the King's war.
{town}'s pulpit turns against the crown.
